items.prompt:
Read the fable.

An ant worked all summer storing food, while a grasshopper played and stored nothing. When winter came, the ant had plenty to eat, but the grasshopper went hungry.

What is the theme of this fable?
A) Summer is short
B) It is wise to prepare for the future
C) Ants are stronger than grasshoppers
D) Playing is bad
items.answer: B) It is wise to prepare for the future

steps: The ant prepares and has food in winter.
The grasshopper does not prepare and goes hungry.
The lesson is to prepare for the future, choice B.
solution.answer: B) It is wise to prepare for the future

items.prompt:
Read the story.

Maya wanted to give up learning the piano after one hard week. Her teacher told her to practice just ten minutes a day. Maya stuck with it, and a month later she played her first whole song.

What lesson does this story teach?
A) Piano is easy
B) Sticking with something leads to progress
C) Teachers are strict
D) Songs are short
items.answer: B) Sticking with something leads to progress

steps: Maya almost quits but keeps practicing a little each day.
A month later she plays a whole song.
The lesson is that sticking with it brings progress, choice B.
solution.answer: B) Sticking with something leads to progress

items.prompt:
Read the story.

Dae found a twenty-dollar bill next to a crying boy who had lost his lunch money. Even though Dae wanted a new comic, he handed the money to the boy. The boy's smile made Dae feel better than any comic could.

What is the theme of this story?
A) Comics are expensive
B) Helping others can make you feel happy
C) Never pick up money
D) Boys cry too much
items.answer: B) Helping others can make you feel happy

steps: Dae gives up the comic to help the boy.
Helping made him feel better than a comic would.
The theme is that helping others brings happiness, choice B.
solution.answer: B) Helping others can make you feel happy

items.prompt:
Read the story.

Rico could run faster than anyone and reminded the team constantly. During the relay, he grabbed the baton and sprinted so far ahead of his own plan that he dropped it at the handoff. The slower but careful runner on the next team passed the baton smoothly and won.

Which statement best expresses the theme?
A) Fast runners always win races
B) Being careful can matter more than being fast
C) Relays need four runners
D) Rico should quit the team
items.answer: B) Being careful can matter more than being fast

steps: Rico is fast but careless and drops the baton.
The careful runner wins by handing off smoothly.
The theme is that carefulness can beat pure speed, choice B.
solution.answer: B) Being careful can matter more than being fast

items.prompt:
Read the story.

On her first day at the shelter, Bianca thought volunteering meant getting to play with puppies. Instead she scrubbed cages, hauled heavy bags, and cleaned up messes. She was tired, but when a shy dog finally wagged its tail at her, she understood why the work mattered.

Which sentence best summarizes the story?
A) Bianca plays with puppies all day and has fun
B) Bianca learns that real volunteering is hard work but rewarding
C) Bianca quits the shelter after one day
D) Bianca adopts a shy dog and takes it home
items.answer: B) Bianca learns that real volunteering is hard work but rewarding

steps: A summary states the main events accurately.
Bianca expects fun but does hard chores, then feels rewarded when a dog trusts her.
Choice B captures this; the others add or change facts.
solution.answer: B) Bianca learns that real volunteering is hard work but rewarding

items.prompt:
Read the poem.

I planted just a single seed
And almost walked away.
I watered it and pulled the weeds
A little every day.
And now a hundred flowers stand
Where bare brown dirt once lay.

What is the theme of the poem?
A) Gardening is messy
B) Small, steady care can create something great
C) Flowers are prettier than dirt
D) One seed is not enough
items.answer: B) Small, steady care can create something great

steps: The speaker cares for one seed "a little every day."
That steady care produces "a hundred flowers."
The theme is that small, steady effort creates something great, choice B.
solution.answer: B) Small, steady care can create something great

items.prompt:
Read the story.

The villagers begged the wise woman for the secret to happiness. She handed each of them a heavy stone and told them to carry it up the hill. Halfway up, exhausted, they wanted to throw the stones down. "Now," she said, "you have discovered it. Happiness is knowing when to set down what weighs you down." The villagers dropped their stones and walked home lighter than ever.

Which statement best expresses the theme?
A) Climbing hills makes people stronger
B) Letting go of burdens can bring peace and happiness
C) Wise women give strange advice
D) Carrying stones is good exercise
items.answer: B) Letting go of burdens can bring peace and happiness

steps: The stones stand for burdens people carry.
The wise woman says happiness is knowing when to set them down.
The theme is that letting go of burdens brings happiness, choice B.
solution.answer: B) Letting go of burdens can bring peace and happiness

items.prompt:
Read the story.

The emperor loved only the golden mechanical bird that sang perfect songs, and he sent the plain gray nightingale away. When he fell ill, he wound the golden bird again and again, but its stiff song brought him no comfort. Then, at his window, the real nightingale returned and sang, and its living song gave the emperor the strength to recover.

Which theme is best supported by the story?
A) Machines never break
B) What is real and living is more valuable than what only looks perfect
C) Emperors should own many birds
D) Gold is the most precious thing
items.answer: B) What is real and living is more valuable than what only looks perfect

steps: The emperor prefers the perfect golden bird and sends the real one away.
The golden bird cannot comfort him, but the living nightingale heals him.
The theme is that what is real and alive is worth more than fake perfection, choice B.
solution.answer: B) What is real and living is more valuable than what only looks perfect
